reason: This passage (Exodus 3) centers on God's self-revelation, compassion for the suffering of enslaved Israelites, and the mandate to liberate them from Egypt. The text emphasizes Yahweh's covenant identity ('I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob'), his response to the cry of the people ('I have heard the cry of the children of Israel... I have seen the oppression with which the Egyptians oppress them'), and his mission of liberation ('I will send you to Pharaoh that you may bring my people, the children of Israel, out of Egypt'). While the passage mentions worship on the mountain as a sign of God's mission, rituals and ceremonies are not the focus or concern driving God's actions in this text.
